summary: Professional-grade operational audit across every app surface, with live-metric grounding

surfaceGrades.summary: The mobile web surface is genuinely solid and has clearly been through several real-operator-driven hardening passes — the three named in-flight bugs (media-picker overlay occlusion, screen-settings drawer clipping, address-picker coverage) are all addressed in current code via a clean systemic overlay-lock pattern, viewport-clamped popovers, and a server-side geocode path. The remaining gaps are efficiency/cost (redundant 10s background fleet polling + direct third-party geocode calls from the browser) and touch-target/iOS-zoom polish in the AssetPicker toolbar, not broken layouts. Strong life-safety panic page. No P0s; the cost issue (P1) matters given Vercel edge requests are already at 88% of plan.
strengths: Panic page (apps/web/src/app/panic/page.tsx) is professional-grade life-safety UX: 3s hold-to-trigger with setPointerCapture so finger-drift doesn't reset the timer (L234-243), keyboard-equivalent hold for motor-impaired users (L249-260), aria-live + Web Speech announcements (L78-96), explicit misconfigured/unauthorized/error phases that tell the operator 'NOTIFY SECURITY MANUALLY — your alert was NOT broadcast' instead of lying, and a dedicated layout that locks zoom (panic/layout.tsx L20-25) so a pinch can't cancel the gesture. This is the right way to build a safety control.

The overlay-lock pattern (hooks/use-overlay-lock.ts) is the correct systemic fix for the 'footer button hidden under the bottom tab bar' class — a reference-counted store so stacked overlays (picker-in-upload, confirm-in-modal) keep the MobileTabBar hidden until the LAST one closes (MobileTabBar.tsx L57, L88). Far better than per-modal padding hacks.

Screen-row list (screens/page.tsx L1892-2063) is carefully reflowed for mobile: a desktop flex row dissolves into a stacked card via three `sm:contents` wrappers, with status pills wrapping onto their own line and 44px-target action buttons (h-11 / h-11 w-11). This is real responsive engineering, not a desktop layout crammed onto a phone.

Screen-settings popover positioning (screens/page.tsx L874-911) clamps the menu fully on-screen at any viewport width and flips above/below based on available space — directly fixing the off-left-edge bug, rendered via createPortal to document.body (L1298) so no overflow-hidden ancestor clips it.
Address picker has a server-first geocode (lib/geocode.ts geocodeViaApi) keeping the Google Maps key server-side, with non-blocking geolocation region-bias that degrades gracefully on denial.

Leaflet fleet map is dynamically imported with ssr:false and a height-matched skeleton (ScreenMapClient.tsx) and list — not map — is the default view on the screens page (L1382), so phones don't pay the map's JS/tile cost unless asked.

Root viewport keeps userScalable:true with maximumScale:5 on the dashboard (layout.tsx L99-104) for low-vision admins, while panic/player lock zoom in their own layouts — the correct per-route a11y nuance.

Mobile drawer (Sidebar.tsx L321-327) uses w-72 max-w-[85vw] with a proper translate/backdrop and h-dvh, and the tab bar respects env(safe-area-inset-bottom) (MobileTabBar.tsx L224) for iPhone home-indicator clearance.

surfaceGrades.summary: The player surface is genuinely well-engineered on reliability, offline resilience, and Taurus/Chromium-83 safety — multi-transport emergency delivery (WS → SSE → adaptive HTTP poll), a thoughtfully-versioned service worker with SHA-256 verify and cache-forward-on-upgrade, exponential-backoff-with-jitter reconnect, and a fail-loud emergency overlay that's correctly stripped of inset/gap/blur. The one serious, quantified defect is telemetry write-amplification: the cache-status and render-proof POSTs each fire an unconditional Screen row UPDATE every 30s with no debounce and (for cache-status) no throttle, which the LIVE pg_stat_statements attributes to ~59% of all DB time — and the fix (the existing shouldSkipLastPingWrite debounce, already applied to the ping/manifest paths) is sitting right next to the offending code. Secondary issues are redundant overlapping heartbeats (3 GET /status loops per playing kiosk feeding the Vercel edge-request pressure) and a 7,875-line / 391 KB single-file player page that is a real maintainability liability.
strengths: Emergency path is defense-in-depth and correct: WS primary, SSE middle tier, and an independent adaptive HTTP poll (5s when emergency active or WS degraded, 10s idle) at apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:4185-4196 — life-safety never rides a single transport. EmergencyOverlay (apps/web/src/components/player/EmergencyOverlay.tsx) is aria-live=assertive, fails LOUD on a 401/403 poll (lines 105-113, fixing a prior silent-swallow bug), and device-JWT-authed.

Taurus/Chromium-83 safety is handled systematically, not ad-hoc. The global inset polyfill in apps/web/src/app/player/layout.tsx:199-215 force-applies longhand sides to any inline inset:0, neutralizing the entire class; EmergencyOverlay explicitly drops gap/blur on the life-safety surface with documented rationale (EmergencyOverlay.tsx:149-159). The dual-declared shorthand+longhand callsites (page.tsx:7678, KioskSplash) follow the documented safe pattern.

The service worker (apps/web/public/sw-player.js) is professional: two cache tiers with a never-evicted emergency floor, real SHA-256 body verification before caching (lines 509-529), cache-forward of emergency/meta/playlist on VERSION bump to avoid fleet-wide re-download (lines 105-165), stable-key dedup that survives Supabase signed-URL token rotation (lines 677-695), and 206-Range synthesis so cached video actually plays offline (lines 181-216).

Reliability hardening shows hard-won field experience: exponential backoff with full jitter capped at 30s (page.tsx:436), WS dead-connection detection at 60s (page.tsx:3808), render-proof via a requestAnimationFrame paint counter that correctly stays SILENT when the compositor is wedged (page.tsx:2508-2513) so a frozen kiosk goes RED instead of falsely green, and bundle-drift self-reload that defers during emergencies and mid-playback (page.tsx:3533-3572).

Server-side write-amplification was already taken seriously on the hot paths: the manifest + status heartbeat both use the 25s shouldSkipLastPingWrite debounce and collapsed 3 round-trips to 1-2 (screens.controller.ts:630-675, manifest-hot-cache.ts) — the infrastructure to fix the remaining telemetry endpoints already exists in-repo.

Preview-mode guards are consistently applied across every telemetry write (cache-status, render-proof, always-on heartbeat) so an admin's browser preview can never write lastPingAt/lastRenderedAt on the real paired device's row — a subtle correctness trap that was clearly anticipated.

surfaceGrades.summary: A maturely-engineered dashboard whose hard-won reliability fixes (favicon-crash class, stale-bundle self-heal, per-tab auth isolation, smart retry/CSRF api-client, honest a11y ratchet) are genuinely professional-grade and battle-scarred in the right way. But it leaves real performance on the table: the entire ~127k-LOC widget tree is eager-loaded on the Templates gallery (the dynamic split is defeated by one static import), nearly every page is a monolithic 'use client' route with almost no code-splitting, and several global-shell queries poll in the background indefinitely — feeding the 88%-of-quota Vercel edge-request problem. Solid B: reliability and code-quality are strong, performance/efficiency and tech-currency drag it down.
strengths: The favicon / React-owned-node crash class is correctly and durably fixed: BrandStyleInjector.setBrandFavicon (BrandStyleInjector.tsx:167-197) mutates the Next-emitted <link rel=icon> nodes in place instead of .remove()-ing them, with an extensive comment explaining the WebKit commitDeletion crash. The remaining removeChild calls (screens/page.tsx:800, client-logger.ts:144, flex-gap-polyfill.ts:43) all operate on nodes the code itself created — not React-owned. This is exactly right.

StaleBundleWatcher (StaleBundleWatcher.tsx) is a thoughtful piece of fleet hygiene: polls /api/build-info every 5min, and freshReload() (line 49) calls registration.update() + deletes only edu-shell-* CacheStorage entries before reloading — solving the 'reload doesn't help, I have to clear cache' SW-staleness bug without wiping the kiosk player's offline store.

The api-client (api-client.ts) is genuinely senior-grade: 5xx retry only on idempotent methods + login (never double-submits mutations, line 112-114), CSRF token auto-attached on mutations, a 401-storm guard (sessionLogoutFired, line 57), an api-status event bus for reconnect banners, and a deliberate decision NOT to force cache:'no-store' (line 83-90) so GETs honor server Cache-Control while React Query owns invalidation.

Per-tab auth isolation via sessionStorage (ui-store.ts:5-25) with a one-time localStorage→sessionStorage migration directly fixes a real multi-tenant identity-bleed across tabs. The reasoning is documented and correct.

React Query defaults (providers.tsx) are well-tuned: 5min staleTime, refetchOnWindowFocus, and an explicit, commented prohibition on a global refetchInterval — showing the team learned from the 2026-04-19 'polling storm' perf incident.

The a11y baseline (scripts/a11y-warning-baseline.json) is honest and DOWN-only ratcheted to a real locked count of 1 warning, with a forthright coverage caveat that the CI harness runs unauthenticated. That intellectual honesty is rare and valuable.

Security headers are set globally in next.config.ts (X-Frame-Options, frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, HSTS) with a documented, defensible reason for deferring a full content CSP. Player/SW cache-control headers are correct and per-route.

Tech stack is near-current: Next 16.2.6, React 19.2.4, Tailwind 4 — and optimizePackageImports is correctly configured for lucide-react, Base UI, dnd-kit, react-query, date-fns to kill barrel-import bloat.

surfaceGrades.summary: A well-engineered Prisma/Postgres layer with disciplined migrations, RLS on all 66 tables, smart in-process caching on the hot manifest and board paths, and an explicit history of fixing N+1/egress issues — clearly maintained by someone who reads query plans. It is held back from an A by one concrete, live-confirmed efficiency defect: ~59% of all DB time is spent on undebounced player-telemetry writes (cache-status + render-proof) that fire every 30s per screen and bypass the very debounce pattern the codebase already uses for lastPingAt. A latent game_events index gap is real but well-mitigated by a 1s board cache.
strengths: Migration discipline is professional-grade: 73 tracked migrations under prisma/migrations, migration_lock.toml committed, `prisma migrate deploy` runs in the boot wrapper (Dockerfile:101 / scripts/railway-start.sh) — no `prisma db push` anywhere in the production path. Schema is the single source of truth.

The manifest hot path is genuinely well-optimized: apps/api/src/screens/manifest-hot-cache.ts implements a 25s in-process lastPingAt write-debounce (shouldSkipLastPingWrite) + a 2s tenant emergency-state read cache, dropping ~100 writes/sec at 500 screens to ~2.5/min/screen. The heartbeat write is wrapped in withDbRetry and uses a tight OTA_SELECT (screens.controller.ts:647-674).

The 750ms board poll — the obvious egress/DB bomb — is defused by a 1s in-process board cache with explicit per-write invalidation (sports.service.ts:421-444, invalidateBoardCache on every record()), so a 50-viewer game hits the DB ~once/sec, not 50×750ms. getBoardFresh also uses an explicit column `select` rather than `SELECT *` (sports.service.ts:451-461).
The ~8 board sub-queries are parallelized via a single Promise.all (sports.service.ts:494-542) — one round-trip latency, not 8 sequential RTTs.

Hot telemetry columns (last_cache_report_at, last_rendered_at) are deliberately NOT indexed (schema.prisma:700-727), which preserves Postgres HOT-update optimization and avoids index write-amplification on every telemetry POST.

Evidence of real query-plan-driven tuning in comments and migrations: 20260423_hot_path_indexes, the emergency-asset query collapsed from 2 RTTs to 1 via include (screens.controller.ts:3335-3342), the emergency-audit-log debounce bumped 15min→6h to cut ~4,800→200 rows/day (manifest-hot-cache.ts:103-107). Multi-pod boot race handled correctly with a Postgres advisory lock that IS released (ensure-system-presets.ts:323/647).

Connection pool is correctly sized per CLAUDE.md (connection_limit=10 + pool_timeout=20 on DATABASE_URL), and a withDbRetry wrapper handles transient pgbouncer hiccups (prisma/with-db-retry.ts). Live metric (28/60 connections, 100% cache hit, 99.98% commit) confirms the pool is healthy.

surfaceGrades.summary: A genuinely well-engineered NestJS backend with strong error-envelope normalization, thoughtful DB-retry/resilience primitives, multi-replica-safe billing reconciliation, and disciplined secret-handling — clearly the product of many hardening passes. It loses a full grade to two concrete launch-class defects (user-deletion 500 via unhandled FK Restrict; the two highest-frequency telemetry writes are unprotected and un-coalesced, accounting for ~59% of all DB time) plus systemic gaps: validation is wired on only ~12 of ~30 controllers, the error-envelope discipline (task #57) is still violated by 200-with-{error} returns, and the background-job/cron fleet is only single-replica safe — a horizontal-scaling landmine. Solid B; reaches A- once the two P0s and validation coverage close.
strengths: AllExceptionsFilter (common/all-exceptions.filter.ts) is professional-grade: a STATUS_CODE_LABELS map gives every HTTP status a stable machine `code`, Prisma P2002/P2025 are mapped to 409/404, stack traces are scrubbed in prod, HttpException messages are author-vetted and exposed, and 5xx (only) are captured to Sentry with route/method/user tags and a traceId returned to the client.

withDbRetry (prisma/with-db-retry.ts) is a genuinely good resilience primitive — transient-only classification by both Prisma code AND message-fragment, exponential backoff with ±20% jitter (explicitly to de-correlate 1000-kiosk retry storms), a 600ms hard wall-clock deadline so heartbeats stay subsecond, and it correctly NEVER retries logic errors (P2002/P2025). Backed by with-db-retry.spec.ts.

PrismaService (prisma/prisma.service.ts) does fire-and-forget $connect with a 5s timeout so a DB blip at boot can't crashloop the container — the right call, and it pairs with /health always-200 liveness.

Multi-replica-safe billing reconciliation: license-reconcile.cron.ts uses an AuditLog-row-as-lease dedup (findFirst for a LICENSE_RECONCILED row today before acting) after explicitly abandoning an unreliable Redis SETNX lock — exactly the right pattern, and Stripe webhooks are idempotent via a processed_stripe_events ledger keyed on evt_* id.

Secret handling: required-secret.ts fails LOUD and FAST in production for missing/empty JWT/SESSION/DEVICE secrets (no more `|| 'default_secret'` fallbacks), and Sentry (sentry.ts) scrubs Authorization/Cookie headers and any secret|token|key|password body/header field before transmit.

trust-proxy is set to exactly 1 hop (main.ts ~line 56) with a detailed comment showing the team understood per-IP throttle degradation to GLOBAL throttle behind a proxy — and per-endpoint @Throttle decorators tighten login/register/ota-state/crash-report beyond the 600/min default.

Zod validation via a custom ZodValidationPipe is wired into the security-sensitive controllers (auth, mfa, emergency, ai, integrations, playlists, schedules, submissions, templates) — the boundaries that matter most are covered.
EfficiencyInterceptor is O(1) per request (Content-Length read, no body serialization, fire-and-forget Redis HINCRBY) — observability without a latency tax.

surfaceGrades.surface: vercel-edge (apps/web/vercel.json, apps/web/src/app/cdn/**, apps/web/src/app/api/** cron-keepwarm/build-info, next.config images/headers/runtimes)
surfaceGrades.summary: The edge/CDN layer is competently built — the SSRF-locked asset proxy that fixed the 5.79 GB Supabase egress incident, content-hashed static caching with explicit no-store on SW + player shell, and security headers are genuinely professional-grade. But the layer carries real cost and reliability debt: the 750 ms polling architecture (no WebSocket on board/ribbon/scorebug) is the structural cost driver, the production NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL→Railway-direct wiring that makes the whole thing work is undocumented and one careless edit away from killing the WS tier fleet-wide, the keepwarm route is orphaned dead code with a lying docstring, and the edge asset proxy has no fetch timeout. The prior audit's claim that the /api/v1/* rewrite drives the 887K edge bill is not supported by the code — polls go direct to Railway.
strengths: SSRF-safe edge asset proxy (cdn/assets/[...path]/route.ts) is genuinely well-engineered: hard-locked to one Supabase bucket via a fixed prefix + per-segment encodeURIComponent (no arbitrary-URL fetch), strips Range so responses are cacheable 200s not 206s, overrides Supabase's no-cache with immutable s-maxage=31536000 — this is the real fix for the documented 98 MB→5.79 GB egress incident and it's done correctly with edge runtime to dodge the 4.5 MB serverless cap.

Cache-Control discipline is correct and intentional: content-hashed /_next/static chunks keep long max-age while the player shell HTML, /sw.js and /sw-player.js are explicitly no-store (next.config.ts:57-96) — this is exactly right for OTA freshness on locked-firmware Android Webview kiosks, and the comments document the real 2026-06-08 stale-SW incident that motivated it.

Security headers on every route (next.config.ts:48-55): X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, frame-ancestors 'self', nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, HSTS with includeSubDomains — a sensible baseline, with an honest comment explaining why a full content CSP is deferred (pervasive inline widget styles need a nonce rollout) rather than shipping a broken one.

apiFetch (api-client.ts) has mature resilience: 502/503/504 retry with 1s/3s/7s backoff, CSRF token on mutations, a single-fire session-logout guard against 401 storms, and a deliberate decision NOT to force cache:'no-store' so React Query + HTTP caches can layer (documented against the 2026-04-19 perf audit).

productionBrowserSourceMaps:false + optimizePackageImports for lucide/base-ui/dnd-kit/react-query/date-fns trims first-paint bundle on the heavy dashboard routes — correct, measured optimizations with rationale.

build-info route is a clean, correct mechanism for stale-bundle detection: server-rendered from the live deployment so old kiosks polling it always see the new SHA, no-store header, graceful null fallback off-Vercel.

surfaceGrades.summary: This is a genuinely mature, heavily-audited security surface — the kind of defense-in-depth you'd expect from a senior team, not a pre-launch startup. Authentication (Argon2id + timing-equalizer, fail-closed JWT verification, dual-secret device/user split, per-user mass revocation), SSRF (connect-time DNS-rebind pin), CSRF (enforce-by-default), audit-log DB-level immutability, and the emergency authorization gate are all implemented to a professional standard with honest, accurate code comments. The remaining gaps are mostly operational/config (rotate weak prod secrets, move floor-plans to a private bucket) plus two real code-level fail-open seams in the JWT-revocation path that contradict the "fail-closed" comments. Not an A because of those revocation seams, the public floor-plan bucket, and a permissive CSP/CORS.
strengths: SSRF defense is best-in-class: apps/api/src/branding/safe-fetch.ts closes the DNS-rebind TOCTOU with a connect-time `lookup` pin (ssrfSafeLookup) that re-validates every resolved address at socket-connect, not just up front — and it deliberately uses node:http(s) instead of global fetch precisely to get that hook. Redirects are re-validated, byte-capped, and webhook POSTs refuse to follow 3xx. This is the single most-commonly-botched control in SaaS and it's done right.

Emergency authorization is rigorous: resolveScopeTenant (emergency.controller.ts:267) resolves the OWNING tenant from the DB row for every scope (tenant/group/device) and denies cross-tenant before any mutation; the override playlistId is independently re-verified against the owning tenant (line 376) to block pasting another tenant's playlist UUID; state-mutation + AuditLog are wrapped in one $transaction so you can never get a CRITICAL status with no forensic trail.

Audit-log immutability is enforced at the storage layer, not just the app: migration 20260531000000 installs a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that blocks all deletes and all content updates, permitting ONLY the FK ON-DELETE-SET-NULL anonymization — and the migration comment correctly explains the user-hard-delete interaction that a naive blanket block would have broken.

Login is timing-safe against email enumeration: auth.service.ts computes a module-load Argon2id dummy hash and verifies against it on user-miss AND on non-ACTIVE-user, equalizing the response time across all three branches (lines 22-27, 61-66, 79-82).

WS emergency fan-out is HMAC-gated server-side at the Redis chokepoint (redis.service.ts:137 verifyWsHmac) with a constant-time compare + freshness window, and the team honestly removed the dead verifyMessage() 'audit theater' rather than leaving a safeguard with zero callers (websocket-signer.service.ts:24-56).

Boot-time fail-closed posture: required-secret.ts throws in production on any missing/short secret; main.ts refuses to boot without ALLOWED_ORIGINS and validates the DATABASE_URL pool config. No `process.env.X || 'default'` fallbacks remain.

The passport-saml CVE-2025-54419 'launch blocker' is already well-mitigated at the dependency level: the package is NOT installed (absent from package.json and node_modules), the require() sites fall through to an honest 503, and the unauthenticated SAML callback is hard-gated on an enabled config (sso.service.ts:316) — exposure is 0 enabled tenants. OIDC enforces state+nonce (sso.service.ts:401).

No secret-in-log leakage: a targeted scan of every console.* call for password/token/secret/bearer found only the harmless randomBytes example string in required-secret.ts. SSO config read-path returns hasSecret booleans, never plaintext (toSafeConfig). SOS location input is CR/LF/TAB-stripped to prevent log-injection (emergency.controller.ts:860).

surfaceGrades.summary: Dependency health is genuinely good for a solo-led startup: a recent, actively-remediated lockfile (passport-saml + tar chain removed in e8de8f96, transitive CVE floors enforced via pnpm.overrides, Dependabot configured monorepo-wide), no abandoned direct deps, and a CI pipeline that is well above typical — it builds the exact Railway Docker image and boot-smokes it. The grade is held below A- by three things: the production runtime still carries deprecated Multer 1.x (directly imported in 3 controllers) alongside the patched 2.x, the platform runs on EOL Node 20 with no version pin anywhere, and major-version currency (Prisma 5, Express 4) is lagging with no staging environment to de-risk those upgrades. None are launch-blocking, but they're the difference between "professional" and "best-in-class."
strengths: Lockfile is actively maintained and security-conscious: pnpm.overrides (package.json:62-69) pins transitive CVE floors (undici>=6.24.0, basic-ftp, fast-uri, fast-xml-parser/builder, tmp>=0.2.6) with a clear comment explaining they're dev-toolchain-only and don't ship to prod. node-fetch@2.7.0 and form-data@4.0.5 resolve to patched versions.

CVE remediation is recent and real, not theater: commit e8de8f96 removed passport-saml (critical CVE-2025-54419) and the tar chain via an argon2 bump; tar is fully gone from the lockfile (0 entries). The SAML critical is correctly mitigated by NOT installing the package — apps/api/src/sso/sso.service.ts:13 documents the intentional require()-fallthrough until task #199 migrates to @node-saml/passport-saml.

CI/CD pipeline is materially above startup norm. deploy-reliability.yml docker-build job (line 179) builds the identical Railway image, runs a 60s boot smoke test with full diagnostic dump on failure, and curls /api/v1/health. Plus lockfile-drift gate, taurus-safety Chromium-83 ratchet, WebKit favicon-crash canary (prod-smoke.yml:97), gitleaks secret scan, and a jsx-a11y baseline ratchet that only goes down.

Dependabot is configured across all 9 package.json directories + GitHub Actions with a deliberate, documented noise policy (.github/dependabot.yml): grouped minor/patch PRs, majors ignored (because argon2/prisma/eslint majors break builds) BUT security updates explicitly bypass the ignore. This is a mature, intentional posture, not neglect.

Core framework stack is current and on supported majors: Next 16.2.6, React 19.2.4, NestJS 11, Tailwind 4, TypeScript 5.7/5.9, Zod 4, Zustand 5, React Query 5, PostgreSQL 17. No legacy EOL libraries as direct deps (no request/moment/node-sass).

Trivy action is supply-chain-hardened: pinned to an immutable commit SHA (ci.yml:216, aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd...v0.36.0) rather than a moveable @master/tag ref, with a comment explaining why.

allFindings.title: Screens page double-polls the whole fleet every 10s in the background — redundant DB load + mobile battery/data drain, against an 88%-full Vercel edge budget
allFindings.fix: The screens page mounts BOTH useScreenGroups() (10s, refetchIntervalInBackground:true, staleTime:0) and useScreens() (10s, refetchIntervalInBackground:true, staleTime:0) — two full fleet fetches every 10s, each ~150 rows. On a phone these fire even when the tab is backgrounded / the screen is off, burning battery, cellular data, and Vercel edge requests (already 88% of plan per the live metrics). Pick ONE source of truth for the list (the page renders status from group.screens[] per the comment at L26-28, so useScreens may be entirely redundant here), drop refetchIntervalInBackground for the mobile case (or gate it on document.visibilityState), and raise staleTime above 0 so focus/reconnect refetches don't stack on the interval. Long-term this is the same 750ms-poll-instead-of-WebSocket pattern flagged in the live metrics — fleet status is a prime candidate for the existing signed-WS channel.

allFindings.title: Address picker still makes direct browser calls to Nominatim + Photon — third-party data leak, OSM ToS violation, and flaky/CORS-fragile on locked-down networks
allFindings.fix: After the server-side geocodeViaApi() path, the modal falls back to fetching photon.komoot.io and nominatim.openstreetmap.org DIRECTLY from the browser on every keystroke (debounced 300ms). This (a) leaks the operator's typed building address + their IP to two third parties on every search, (b) violates Nominatim's usage policy, which explicitly forbids autocomplete/keystroke querying and an unset Referer/UA from a public app, so it will get rate-limited or blocked at scale, and (c) is the most likely root cause of the 'address picker not finding US addresses' report — these endpoints are frequently blocked by school/corporate firewalls and CORS proxies, and they fail silently to setNoMatch. Move BOTH providers behind the existing /api/v1/geocode proxy (server-side, with a proper User-Agent and the merge/dedupe logic that already exists in the modal) so the only origin the browser talks to is your own API. That also unifies the 'no match' behavior and lets you cache repeat lookups.

allFindings.title: AssetPicker toolbar controls are sub-44px and the folder <select> is 12px text — fails touch-target minimum and triggers iOS Safari auto-zoom on focus
allFindings.fix: Unlike the screen rows, the AssetPicker's mobile toolbar was never reflowed. The folder <select> (text-xs + py-1.5 ≈ 28px tall) and the 'Upload new' button (py-1.5 ≈ 28px) are both well under the 44px target and sit in a single cramped non-wrapping flex row. Worse, text-xs (12px) on the <select> is below iOS Safari's 16px threshold, so tapping it auto-zooms the viewport and the operator has to pinch back out — exactly the kind of friction the 30-second-happy-path rule targets, and this picker is the entry point for nearly every image/logo/sponsor upload. Bump the select + button to min-h-[44px] and set the select's font to text-base/16px on mobile (text-base sm:text-xs), and let the toolbar wrap on narrow widths.

allFindings.title: Template builder is hard-gated off all phones with a 'larger screen required' wall, undercutting the 'run the whole show from your phone' promise
allFindings.fix: Any /templates/builder/* route renders a full-screen 'needs at least 1024px' block on <lg viewports with no mobile fallback at all. That's a defensible call for the drag-and-drop canvas, but it means a sports/QSR operator who is told the product needs 'no laptop' literally cannot touch a template from their phone — not even to fix a typo. Consider a read-only / text-only mobile editing mode (the field-level PropertiesPanel edits don't need the canvas), or at minimum soften the wall on tablet-portrait (768-1024px) where the builder is closer to usable. Not launch-blocking, but it contradicts the stated positioning.

allFindings.title: cache-status + render-proof telemetry do an unconditional Screen UPDATE every 30s with no debounce — ~59% of all DB time
evidence: apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3242-3248 (reportCacheStatus: unconditional screen.update of lastCacheReport JSON + lastCacheReportAt every call, no shouldSkipLastPingWrite, no @Throttle)

apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3302-3309 (reportRenderProof: unconditional screen.update of lastRenderedAt every call; @Throttle 10/min exists but does not reduce the steady-state 30s write)
apps/api/src/screens/manifest-hot-cache.ts:82-94 (shouldSkipLastPingWrite/markLastPingWritten debounce that the ping+manifest paths use but these two endpoints do NOT)
LIVE pg_stat_statements: UPDATE screens last_cache_report = 41.6% of DB time / 180826 calls; UPDATE screens last_rendered_at = 17.4% / 161168 calls
allFindings.fix: The cache-status payload is identical on ~99% of polls (cache contents rarely change) and render-proof only needs server-clock freshness, so both are writing the same value every 30s. (1) cache-status: gate the write behind a same-as-last-value check (compare the new JSON to the stored lastCacheReport; skip the update when unchanged, OR add a 5-minute debounce keyed by screenId in manifest-hot-cache.ts — admin visibility tolerates 5-min staleness fine) and raise the client cadence to 5 min. (2) render-proof: apply the existing 25s shouldSkipLastPingWrite-style debounce (a fresh-enough lastRenderedAt does not need re-writing every 30s; a 60-90s debounce keeps the render-STALE threshold accurate) and/or use a raw `UPDATE ... SET last_rendered_at = now() WHERE id = $1` to avoid Prisma's full-row rewrite. Either change alone removes the bulk of the 59% DB-time spend with zero behavioral regression.

allFindings.title: Three overlapping GET /screens/status heartbeats per playing kiosk (web 30s + web 45s + native 30s) — redundant network + Vercel edge-request pressure
evidence: apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:3625 (playing-phase httpHeartbeat, setInterval 45_000 — runs concurrently with the always-on loop once phase==='playing')
LIVE Vercel: Edge Requests 887K/1M (88%) — every /api/v1/* is rewritten through Vercel edge
allFindings.fix: In the playing phase the always-on 30s loop already covers liveness, so the additional 45s playing-phase ping at page.tsx:3617-3625 is pure duplication — remove it (the always-on loop's handleHeartbeatOta already processes the OTA fields). For the APK, the native HeartbeatService duplicates the WebView heartbeat; pick ONE (prefer the native one since it survives a wedged WebView) and have the web side skip its own /status ping when running inside the APK (the EduCmsNative bridge is already detected elsewhere). Net: ~3 status GETs/min/kiosk → 1, directly trimming both Vercel edge requests and pooled DB read load at fleet scale.

allFindings.title: player/page.tsx is a 7,875-line / 391 KB single client component — maintainability and bundle-size liability
evidence: Dozens of independent concerns in one file: pairing poll, WS connect, SSE fallback, HTTP fallback, 3 heartbeat loops, cache-status, render-proof, rAF paint counter, bundle-drift reloader, emergency cache refresh, slide cycler, OTA handling
allFindings.fix: This file ships in full to every kiosk's first paint. Extract the cohesive subsystems into hooks/modules (useEmergencyTransport, useTelemetry, useOtaHeartbeat, useBundleDrift, useSlideCycle) — they already communicate via refs so the boundaries are clean. Beyond readability/test-surface, splitting lets Next code-split the rarely-hit paths (pairing, OTA) out of the steady-state playback bundle, shrinking the cold-start payload on low-spec Taurus/Goodview WebViews.

allFindings.title: rAF paint-counter loop runs forever even when no operator content is rendering
evidence: apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:2486-2497 (requestAnimationFrame loop with no gate on render state; comment at 2482-2485 explicitly says it is intentionally always-on)
allFindings.fix: Low impact (a modulo increment per frame), but on a battery-less always-on kiosk it keeps the compositor scheduling rAF callbacks even on the pairing/connecting splash. Optional: pause the loop (return without re-scheduling) when phase is not 'playing'/'emergency', resuming it from the render-state effect. Leave as-is if the team prefers a continuous liveness signal — flagging for awareness, not as a defect.

allFindings.title: Templates gallery eager-loads the entire ~127k-LOC widget tree, defeating the dynamic split that exists elsewhere
evidence: apps/web/src/components/widgets/WidgetRenderer.tsx — 156 static `./` widget imports (every theme, every sport widget, every portrait variant)

apps/web/src/components/templates/ScaledTemplateThumbnail.tsx:29-30 — the SAME WidgetPreview is correctly lazy-loaded via `dynamic(() => import('@/components/widgets/WidgetRenderer'))`, with a comment explaining it exists to avoid 'dragging that entire bundle in'
allFindings.fix: Replace the static `import { WidgetPreview }` on templates/page.tsx:28 with the same `next/dynamic` wrapper ScaledTemplateThumbnail already uses (ssr:false, a small loading skeleton). The gallery renders thumbnails via ScaledTemplateThumbnail (already split) and only needs the heavy WidgetPreview for the live full-size preview modal/pane — load it on demand. This removes the largest first-paint chunk from the most-visited operator route.

allFindings.title: Background polling on the global shell + per-page hooks runs indefinitely in hidden tabs, feeding the 88%-of-quota Vercel edge-request problem
evidence: apps/web/src/hooks/use-api.ts:15-17 — useTenantStatus polls /tenants every 30s with `refetchIntervalInBackground: true`; this hook mounts in the global shell (Sidebar.tsx:54, TopToolbar.tsx:30, DashboardLayout.tsx:24)
apps/web/src/hooks/use-api.ts:33-34 — useScreenGroups polls every 10s with `refetchIntervalInBackground: true` and `staleTime: 0`
Every /api/v1/* request is rewritten through Vercel edge (per session metrics: 887K/1M edge requests, 88%) — each background poll is an edge request even when the operator's tab is hidden all day
allFindings.fix: Drop `refetchIntervalInBackground: true` on the dashboard hooks (keep it only where genuinely needed, e.g. the live sports board). A backgrounded operator tab does not need a 10-30s emergency-status fallback poll — the foreground refetchOnWindowFocus already covers the moment they return. Combined with moving board/ribbon's 750ms poll (board/[gameId]/page.tsx:192) to the WebSocket push path that already exists, this is the highest-leverage edge-cost reduction available.

allFindings.title: `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` on the [schoolId] layout opts EVERY authenticated route out of static optimization
evidence: The layout is `'use client'` (line 1) and gates all chrome behind a `mounted` flag (line 71-83), so there is no server data to render anyway — the force-dynamic was added to silence a Next 16 useParams()-in-client-layout 500 (documented line 8-17)
allFindings.fix: This is a defensible band-aid, but it means the shell HTML is regenerated per request with no caching benefit. Longer term: move the `useParams()`-driven tenant-id read out of the layout (pass schoolId down from a thin server layout, or read it in a client child), then drop force-dynamic so the authed shell can be statically shipped and hydrated. Low urgency given the shell renders an empty placeholder server-side, but it's the kind of thing a perf-conscious team revisits.

allFindings.title: JWT is stored in JS-readable sessionStorage and sent as a Bearer header — XSS-exposed, and contradicts the CLAUDE.md 'HttpOnly cookies' claim
evidence: apps/web/src/store/ui-store.ts:27,43 — token persisted in sessionStorage under `edu_cms_token`
apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts:69,106 — token read from the store and attached as `Authorization: Bearer ${token}`
apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts:102 — `credentials: 'include'` IS set, so cookies are also sent (defense in depth exists), but the Bearer token remains independently exfiltratable by any XSS
allFindings.fix: This is a deliberate tradeoff for per-tab multi-tenant isolation (documented in ui-store.ts:5-25), so it's not a hair-on-fire issue given credentials:'include' already rides cookies. But: (a) update CLAUDE.md / docs to stop claiming the dashboard auth is HttpOnly-cookie-only — it's cookie + JS-readable Bearer; (b) since cookies are already sent, evaluate dropping the sessionStorage token entirely and relying on the HttpOnly cookie for the dashboard (keep Bearer only where a cookie can't ride, e.g. cross-origin), which closes the XSS-token-theft surface without losing per-tab isolation (use a non-sensitive per-tab tenant id instead).

allFindings.title: No cutting-edge Next 16 / React 19 perf features adopted (PPR, React Compiler, dynamicIO/cacheComponents)
evidence: apps/web/next.config.ts:99-115 — experimental block contains only optimizePackageImports; no `ppr`, `reactCompiler`, `dynamicIO`/`cacheComponents`
apps/web/next.config.ts — React 19.2.4 + Next 16.2.6 are current enough to opt into the React Compiler (auto-memoization) and PPR
allFindings.fix: Given the dashboard is almost entirely 'use client' with large components (PropertiesPanel.tsx is 10,336 LOC, WidgetRenderer 4,226), the React Compiler is the single highest-value adoption: enable `experimental.reactCompiler` to get automatic memoization across the heavy builder/widget trees without hand-writing useMemo/useCallback. PPR has lower ROI here because the authed shell is force-dynamic and client-gated — note it as a candidate only after the force-dynamic layout cleanup above.

allFindings.title: App-router pages are overwhelmingly 'use client' monoliths with almost no per-route code-splitting
evidence: 25 of 34 [schoolId] page.tsx files are top-line 'use client' (full route trees ship to the browser)
apps/web/src/app/[schoolId]/templates/page.tsx — 3,344 LOC single client file; playlists/page.tsx 3,056; screens/page.tsx 2,383; settings/page.tsx 1,427
Only 3 `next/dynamic` usages exist across 433 .tsx files (CustomScoreboardScene, ScreenMapClient, ScaledTemplateThumbnail) — code-splitting is the exception, not the norm
31 raw `` tags in app pages vs 1 `next/image` import — no automatic image optimization/lazy-loading on operator pages
allFindings.fix: Split the heaviest interactive surfaces behind next/dynamic where they're conditionally rendered (e.g. the PlaylistCreateWizard, the template preview modal, the PropertiesPanel sub-editors load only when a panel opens). For the 'use client' sprawl, peel the static framing of a few large pages into server components and keep only the interactive islands client-side. Migrate raw `` to next/image (or at minimum add loading='lazy' + width/height) on gallery/asset surfaces to cut layout shift and bytes.

allFindings.title: Player telemetry writes (cache-status + render-proof) are undebounced — 59% of all DB time
evidence: apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3242-3248 (cache-status: unconditional screen.update on every 30s POST, no debounce, no withDbRetry)
apps/api/src/screens/manifest-hot-cache.ts:82-94 (the shouldSkipLastPingWrite debounce that lastPingAt uses but these two endpoints do NOT)
allFindings.fix: These two endpoints write the same `screens` row that lastPingAt already keeps fresh, but with zero coalescing — live pg_stat_statements shows them at 41.6% (180,826 calls, 19.84ms mean) and 17.4% (161,168 calls, 9.33ms mean) of total DB time. Apply the existing debounce pattern: gate both writes behind a per-screen `shouldSkip*Write(id)` check (e.g. 60-120s window for cache-status, which only feeds an admin visibility pill, and ~90s for render-proof, whose staleness threshold is minutes not seconds). Keep the freshest in-memory value and flush on the debounce boundary. This is a ~5-10× reduction on the two hottest queries with no loss of signal fidelity, mirroring the lastPingAt fix already shipped. Also wrap both in withDbRetry for parity with the heartbeat path. The 9-20ms mean on a single-row update of a 76-column table also points at lock contention from these concurrent same-row writers — debouncing directly relieves it.

allFindings.title: game_events index omits `type` — every board sub-query is a per-type scan+sort (33.5% seq scans)
evidence: apps/api/src/sports/sports.service.ts:317-390 (5 latest* helpers, each WHERE gameId=? AND type=? ORDER BY createdAt DESC)
allFindings.fix: The composite index `(gameId, createdAt)` cannot serve the `type` predicate, so Postgres reads all events for the game and filters/sorts in memory — confirmed by the live 33.5% seq-scan ratio on game_events. Add `@@index([gameId, type, createdAt])` so the latest-of-type lookups become an index range scan with no sort. This is currently well-mitigated by the 1s board cache (sports.service.ts:421-444) so it only bites on live-game writes, but the event log grows unbounded per game (append-only undo rail + cue history), so the scan cost rises over a long game / season. Cheap, additive migration; do it before the cache ever has to be loosened. Consider also a retention/compaction job for closed games' event logs.

allFindings.title: screens table is a 76-column wide row absorbing high-frequency single-field telemetry updates
evidence: packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:700-727 (last_cache_report Json, last_rendered_at, last_rendered_frames, last_rendered_hash and ~70 other columns on Screen)
allFindings.fix: Mixing slow-changing config (name, resolution, brand, OTA state, geo, board surface) with high-churn telemetry (lastPingAt, lastCacheReport(At), lastRendered*) on one row means every telemetry POST rewrites a wide tuple and competes for the same row lock. The HOT-update optimization (no index on the churn columns — already done correctly) helps, but the long-term fix is to split high-frequency liveness/telemetry into a narrow `screen_telemetry` sidecar table (1:1 with Screen) so config reads/writes never contend with the 30s telemetry firehose. Lower priority than the debounce — debouncing first removes most of the write volume — but this is the structurally correct shape at fleet scale (the architecture targets 'thousands of screens').

allFindings.title: listGames / listActive-style reads lack pagination and pull full rows
evidence: apps/api/src/sports/sports.service.ts:303-307 (listGames: findMany by tenantId, no take/skip, no select — returns every column of every game ever created for the tenant)
allFindings.fix: listGames returns all games for a tenant ordered by createdAt desc with no `take` limit and no field projection. For a venue running daily games this is unbounded growth on an admin list view. Add a default `take` (e.g. 50) + cursor pagination and an explicit `select` of only the columns the list UI renders. Same projection discipline that getBoardFresh already models (sports.service.ts:451-461) should be applied to the other findMany list endpoints. Verify the `(tenantId, status)`/`(tenantId, createdAt)` index covers the order-by to avoid a sort.

allFindings.title: User deletion 500s on any tenant with real history — unhandled FK Restrict (P2003)
evidence: apps/api/src/common/all-exceptions.filter.ts:107-126 (P2003 absent from switch → falls to DATABASE_ERROR 500)
allFindings.fix: Seven User relations have no onDelete and default to Restrict, so user.delete throws Prisma P2003 the moment the user authored an audit log, uploaded an asset, created a template, or submitted for review (i.e. essentially every real admin). The just-created AuditLog row in the same tx ALSO points at the actor, so it can fail even on a 'clean' user. Two-part fix: (1) decide reassign-vs-null per relation and set onDelete (SetNull for Asset.uploadedByUserId/Template.createdById/Submission.submittedById after making them nullable, or block deletion with a clear 409 if the user owns assets) and add a migration; (2) map P2003 in all-exceptions.filter.ts to HTTP 409 CONFLICT with a `code:'FK_CONSTRAINT'` so it never surfaces as an opaque 500. Add a users.service spec that deletes a user with audit/asset/template history.

allFindings.title: The two highest-frequency writes (cache-status, render-proof) are unprotected by withDbRetry and un-coalesced — ~59% of all DB time
evidence: apps/api/src/prisma/with-db-retry.ts:7-17 (header: 'bad for the high-frequency, kiosk-driven endpoints (status heartbeat, manifest fetch) where a 500 cascade can flip a fleet to OFFLINE')
LIVE METRIC: UPDATE screens last_cache_report = 41.6% of DB time / 180826 calls / 19.84ms mean; UPDATE screens last_rendered_at = 17.4% / 161168 calls / 9.33ms mean
allFindings.fix: These are the exact endpoints withDbRetry was built to protect, yet only the status heartbeat (screens.controller.ts:545) and pairing got wrapped — cache-status and render-proof did not. Two issues: (1) wrap both update calls in withDbRetry so a transient pgbouncer blip doesn't 500 a frozen-screen alert; (2) the write amplification itself is the cost driver — each kiosk POSTs cache-status + render-proof on a fixed cadence and each does a full-row UPDATE on the wide `screens` table (plus cache-status does a redundant findUnique first). Coalesce telemetry into a separate narrow `screen_telemetry` table (or use updateMany with a select to drop the findUnique round-trip), and debounce server-side (only write if >N seconds since last, or batch via a short in-memory flush window). Cutting these two writes would reclaim the majority of DB time per the pg_stat_statements profile.

allFindings.title: Error-envelope discipline (task #57) still violated — controllers return HTTP 200 with bare {error} bodies
evidence: apps/api/src/playlists/playlists.controller.ts:195,216,355 (return { error: 'Not found' } — HTTP 200, no code/message envelope)
apps/api/src/users/users.controller.ts:446-449 (comment documents this exact class: 'error responses were returning 200 with { error } bodies, which let callers swallow the failure')
allFindings.fix: These bare returns are SUCCESSFUL handler returns, so they never reach AllExceptionsFilter — they emit HTTP 200 with `{error:'Not found'}` and no `code`. A client checking status sees success; a client reading `.code` gets undefined. This is the precise defect task #57 tracks and that users.controller.ts already fixed locally. Replace every `return { error: ... }` with `throw new NotFoundException(...)` / appropriate HttpException so the filter normalizes status + the stable `code`. Grep `return.*{ *error:` across all *.controller.ts (hits in at least playlists, screen-groups, screens, templates, asset-files) and fix each.

allFindings.title: Validation coverage is partial — no global ValidationPipe, ~18 controllers accept raw @Body() with no schema
evidence: apps/api/src/app.module.ts:219-222 (global APP_PIPE is SanitizationPipe, not ValidationPipe)
ZodValidationPipe wired on only 12 controllers (ai, auth, mfa, bugs, emergency, integrations, onboarding, playlists, schedules, screen-groups, submissions, templates)
apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3234 (cache-status @Body() body: {...} cast as any, no schema)
allFindings.fix: Security-critical boundaries (auth, emergency, billing) are covered, but ~18 controllers (screens telemetry, tenants, users mutations, stats, hardware, floor-plans, etc.) take untyped @Body() and cast `as any`. The SanitizationPipe HTML-sanitizes strings but does NOT validate shape/types — a malformed body reaches Prisma and surfaces as a 500. Define a Zod schema per mutating endpoint and apply ZodValidationPipe (the infra already exists), prioritizing device-public endpoints (cache-status, ota-state, crash-report, register/pair) since those take unauthenticated-adjacent input. Consider this the close-out of the validation half of task #57.

allFindings.title: Background services + pos/clever crons are only single-replica safe — horizontal-scaling landmine
evidence: apps/api/src/player-ota/canary-auto-promote.ts:49 (setInterval, in-process guard only — writes AuditLog + flips canary on promote)
Contrast: apps/api/src/billing/license-reconcile.cron.ts:207-215 (DB-row lease — the CORRECT cross-replica pattern, already in the codebase)
allFindings.fix: Currently moot at numReplicas:1, but the moment the team scales to 2 replicas (a one-line change), offline-scanner, canary-auto-promote, pos-sync, and clever-sync all double-fire — canary-auto-promote would race two replicas promoting the same tenant and writing duplicate AuditLog rows. license-reconcile.cron.ts already demonstrates the fix in-repo: gate each tick behind a DB-row-as-lease (or a pg advisory lock like ensure-system-presets.ts:323 uses at boot). Port that pattern to all four interval jobs before ever bumping numReplicas. Low effort now, prevents a silent data-integrity bug at scale.

allFindings.title: Two global exception filters registered — redundant Sentry capture + ambiguous ordering
allFindings.fix: AllExceptionsFilter already does Sentry capture for 5xx, so the additional SentryGlobalFilter (APP_FILTER) is redundant and creates two @Catch-all filters in the chain with non-obvious precedence. Pick one: either drop the SentryGlobalFilter provider and keep AllExceptionsFilter as the sole normalizer (preferred — it owns the envelope), or remove the manual Sentry.captureException from AllExceptionsFilter and let SentryGlobalFilter handle capture while AllExceptionsFilter only normalizes. As-is it works but risks double-reporting the same exception to Sentry and confuses future maintainers about which filter shapes the response.

allFindings.title: requireSecret validates length only, not entropy — weak prod secret passes the boot gate
evidence: MEMORY/known-items: 'weak prod JWT/SESSION secrets need rotation' (still open)
allFindings.fix: The boot gate only checks length >= 16, so a dictionary-ish 16-char string passes and the documented weak prod JWT/SESSION secret stays in place. Add a low-entropy reject (e.g. require >= 32 chars for JWT/SESSION/DEVICE secrets, reject if it matches the dev-fallback constants, optionally a Shannon-entropy floor). This is config remediation, not a code rewrite — but the gate that's supposed to catch it currently won't.

allFindings.title: Prisma 5.12 is a full major behind (6.x GA) and ~10 minors stale within 5.x
evidence: LIVE METRIC laggards: Prisma 5.12 (6 is out), Express 4 (5 GA), Node 20 (22 LTS)
allFindings.fix: Prisma 5.12.1 misses ~10 patch/perf releases within 5.x (5.22 is current 5.x) and is a major behind 6.x, which ships query-engine perf improvements and the driver-adapter path relevant to the pgbouncer setup. Bump to latest 5.x first (low-risk, captures perf + bugfixes), then plan the 6.x major behind a branch with the full test suite. Pair with the Express 4→5 and Node 20→22 upgrades tracked in the metrics. Not urgent, but a real product accrues these as tech debt.

allFindings.title: Production NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL→Railway-direct is the load-bearing config that makes the edge cost AND the WS tier work, yet it's undocumented in vercel.json and one edit from a fleet-wide outage
evidence: apps/web/vercel.json:3-8 (rewrites ALL /api/v1/* to Railway, but this is a fallback path only)
apps/web/src/lib/api-url.ts:16 (API_URL = NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL || localhost; all apiFetch + board/ribbon/scorebug polls use this DIRECT url, NOT the rewrite)

docs/research/2026-06-09-prelaunch-final-audit/01-emergency-realtime.md:75 (documents that pointing the env at the venue-os.app proxy would silently kill the WS tier fleet-wide — SSE/poll would mask it)
allFindings.fix: Add a top comment in vercel.json stating the rewrite is a fallback only and that production MUST set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL to the DIRECT Railway origin (never the venue-os.app proxy) or WS upgrades 404 and every poll floods the edge. Add a prod-smoke probe that asserts wss://<api-origin>/realtime returns 101 and that the deployed bundle's baked API URL is the Railway host, failing the deploy if it regressed to the proxy domain.

allFindings.title: 750 ms fixed polling on board/ribbon/scorebug is the structural cost/reliability driver — 3 surfaces × ~80 polls/min/game, no WebSocket push, no backoff when idle
allFindings.fix: These polls hit Railway directly (good — they don't touch the edge), so the cost lands on the API/DB, not Vercel. But 750 ms unconditional polling is wasteful when nothing's changing and it correlates with the DB write-amplification noted in the live metrics. Move live game-state to the existing WS tier with the 750 ms poll as a fallback only, or at minimum back off to 3-5 s when the game clock is stopped / status is PRE/FINAL. A single shared poller (one fetch fanned out to board+ribbon+scorebug on the same machine) instead of three independent setIntervals would cut redundant requests 3x where surfaces share an origin.

allFindings.title: Weak production JWT/SESSION secrets still in use (config blocker) — boot guard validates length, not entropy
evidence: LIVE METRICS: 'weak prod JWT/SESSION secrets need rotation'
allFindings.fix: This is an operational blocker the code cannot self-detect: requireSecret() only enforces presence + >=16 chars, so a weak-but-long secret passes. Rotate JWT_SECRET, SESSION_SECRET, DEVICE_SECRET_KEY, DEVICE_JWT_SECRET on Railway to fresh 64-char hex (`node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"`). Rotating JWT_SECRET invalidates all live user sessions (acceptable). Optionally raise the bar in code: pass `minLength: 32` for these four and/or add a Shannon-entropy / dictionary check so a weak value fails boot too.

allFindings.title: JWT revocation check fails OPEN when Redis is down, contradicting the 'fail-closed' guard comment
evidence: apps/api/src/auth/jwt-auth.guard.ts:97-126 (comment: 'Now we fail CLOSED ... if we can't confirm the token isn't revoked, we deny')
allFindings.fix: The guard's try/catch only fails-closed on THROWN errors, but sismember() swallows the Redis-down case and returns false (= 'not revoked'), and getTokenInvalidBefore() returns null (= 'no mass-revocation marker') — so when Redis is unavailable, a logged-out or demoted user's token keeps working. That directly contradicts the documented intent. Decide the posture explicitly: either make sismember/getTokenInvalidBefore throw a distinguishable RedisUnavailableError when `!connected` so the guard's existing catch fails closed (it already maps to 'Auth check unavailable; please retry'), or keep fail-open but update the guard comment to stop claiming fail-closed. For a life-safety/multi-tenant product, failing closed on revocation is the correct call.

allFindings.title: Floor-plan images stored in a PUBLIC Supabase bucket; signed-URL read path is a fig leaf
evidence: apps/api/src/floor-plans/floor-plans.controller.ts:463-468 (comment 'if it ever escapes the public bucket', `publicUrl = await this.storage.upload(...)`)
task #200 still pending: 'Move floor-plan objects to a PRIVATE Supabase bucket (full F-1 fix)'
allFindings.fix: Floor plans are sensitive (building layouts used for emergency/lockdown response). They upload to a public bucket, so the createSignedUrl TTL on the read path provides no real confidentiality — the object is reachable by anyone with the public URL (leaked via logs, referrer, browser history, or path-guessing within the tenant prefix). Move floor-plan storage to a private bucket and serve exclusively via short-TTL signed URLs (the read path already does this). The tenant-scoped path only mitigates blind guessing, not URL leakage.

allFindings.title: CSRF is bypassed for ALL Bearer-token requests — safe today, but a latent footgun if any cookie-auth mutation route is added
evidence: apps/api/src/security/csrf.middleware.ts:137-144 (CSRF cookie is httpOnly:false by necessity for the double-submit pattern)
allFindings.fix: The Bearer-bypass reasoning is correct (browsers don't auto-attach Bearer headers cross-site, so those requests aren't CSRF-able) and it solves the real Safari-ITP third-party-cookie problem. The latent risk: the dashboard ALSO runs an express-session cookie (main.ts:108) — if any future mutation route is protected by that cookie alone (no Bearer), and the client happens to send a Bearer too, CSRF silently won't apply. Add a CI/lint assertion that no mutation route relies on the session cookie for authz, or document that session cookies are non-authoritative for mutations. Low risk now; flagging so it isn't forgotten.

allFindings.title: Helmet CSP and dev CORS are broad: script/frame/img allow http:+https: and dev CORS allows any *.vercel.app
evidence: apps/api/src/main.ts:86-94 (frameSrc/imgSrc/mediaSrc allow 'http:' and 'https:'; CSP has no upgrade-insecure-requests)
apps/api/src/main.ts:186-201 (dev CORS fallback allows any origin ending in .vercel.app / .ngrok / .trycloudflare)
allFindings.fix: The wide CSP is partly justified (iframe template previews, cross-origin images), and scriptSrc is correctly locked to 'self' (no unsafe-inline/eval) which is the part that matters most for XSS. Two tightenings worth making: (1) drop 'http:' from frameSrc/imgSrc/mediaSrc in production and add `upgrade-insecure-requests` so mixed content can't downgrade; (2) the dev-only CORS `.vercel.app` wildcard is gated behind `!ALLOWED_ORIGINS` and main.ts:145 throws in prod if ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset, so prod is safe — but confirm no preview/staging deploy runs with NODE_ENV!=production AND a real DB, which would expose the wildcard against live data.

allFindings.title: API-key verification uses a non-constant-time hash compare (acknowledged, academic)
evidence: apps/api/src/api-keys/api-keys.service.ts:175-180 (comment concedes timingSafeEqual 'would be ideal'; uses `incomingHash !== row.hashedSecret`)
allFindings.fix: Genuinely low risk and the code comment reasons it correctly: the lookup is by unique prefix, the compared values are SHA-256 hashes of high-entropy 32-hex secrets, and the attacker has no way to iterate toward a hash they don't know. Still, the fix is two lines and removes the asterisk: `crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(incomingHash), Buffer.from(row.hashedSecret))` (lengths are always equal for SHA-256 hex). Worth doing for hygiene/audit-cleanliness rather than exploitability.

allFindings.title: Deprecated Multer 1.x ships to production runtime alongside patched 2.x
evidence: pnpm-lock.yaml:6949 (deprecated: Multer 1.x is impacted by a number of vulnerabilities, which have been patched in 2.x)
allFindings.fix: The API pins multer ^1.4.5-lts.1 (resolves to the deprecated 1.4.5-lts.2) and imports memoryStorage from it in 3 upload controllers, while @nestjs/platform-express@11.1.19 already bundles the patched multer@2.1.1 — so the dependency tree carries both and the operator-facing upload config path runs on the vulnerable 1.x. This collapses the tree to a single patched multer and clears the deprecation warning.

allFindings.title: Production runs on EOL Node 20 with no version pin anywhere in the repo
evidence: no .nvmrc and no "engines" field in any package.json (verified absent)
allFindings.fix: Node 20 is in maintenance/EOL territory (active LTS ended; 22 is the current LTS, 24 the new active line). allFindings.title: No staging environment — the live production deploy is the first integration test
evidence: railway.json:24-27 (single deploy target, numReplicas: 1, no environment split)
.github/workflows/prod-smoke.yml:71-72 (PROD_SMOKE_BASE: https://venue-os.app — smoke runs against LIVE prod, post-deploy)
apps/edge/wrangler.toml:52 has an [env.staging] for the edge worker only — the API/web have no equivalent
allFindings.fix: There is no dev→staging→prod promotion gate; pushes to master deploy straight to the customer-facing Railway API + Vercel web, and prod-smoke.yml only validates AFTER the live deploy is already serving real tenants (Chardon HS, AGC, the water-polo pilot). For a life-safety/emergency product with active pilots this is the single biggest ops-maturity gap. Stand up a Railway 'staging' environment (Railway supports multiple environments natively) + a Vercel preview/staging alias, point a copy of prod-smoke at it, and gate master→prod promotion on staging-smoke-green. This de-risks the very Prisma 5→6 / Node 20→22 / Express 4→5 major upgrades that are currently blocked precisely because there's nowhere safe to test them.

allFindings.title: Container CVE scan (Trivy) and API Jest suite are both non-blocking in the deploy pipeline
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:217 (Trivy: continue-on-error: true — CRITICAL/HIGH OS+library CVEs in the prod image do not fail CI)
.github/workflows/deploy-reliability.yml:138 (API tests: continue-on-error: true — argon2 native binding not built on the raw runner)

allFindings.title: Major-version laggards: Prisma 5, plus type/runtime skew (@types/express@5 over Express 4)
evidence: packages/database/package.json:15,21 (@prisma/client + prisma ^5.12.1 → resolves 5.22.0; Prisma 6 GA, 7 in progress)
.github/dependabot.yml:29-31 (all majors ignored, so these never auto-surface)
allFindings.fix: The ignore-all-majors Dependabot policy is sound for noise, but it means major currency is entirely manual and is silently slipping. (1) Prisma 5.22 → 6 is a worthwhile maintenance bump (perf + better connection handling, relevant given the screens-telemetry write-amplification noted in DB metrics); schedule it on a branch once staging exists. (2) apps/api devDep @types/express is pinned to ^5 while the actual running Express is 4.x (NestJS 11 still ships Express 4) — the type definitions don't match the runtime API surface and can mask or invent signature errors.
