Add a quarterly 'major-bump review' line to the existing hygiene/preflight discipline so laggards get a scheduled look instead of drifting indefinitely.

confirmedCritical.title: Screens page double-polls the whole fleet every 10s in the background — redundant DB load + mobile battery/data drain, against an 88%-full Vercel edge budget
confirmedCritical.fix: The screens page mounts BOTH useScreenGroups() (10s, refetchIntervalInBackground:true, staleTime:0) and useScreens() (10s, refetchIntervalInBackground:true, staleTime:0) — two full fleet fetches every 10s, each ~150 rows. On a phone these fire even when the tab is backgrounded / the screen is off, burning battery, cellular data, and Vercel edge requests (already 88% of plan per the live metrics). Pick ONE source of truth for the list (the page renders status from group.screens[] per the comment at L26-28, so useScreens may be entirely redundant here), drop refetchIntervalInBackground for the mobile case (or gate it on document.visibilityState), and raise staleTime above 0 so focus/reconnect refetches don't stack on the interval. Long-term this is the same 750ms-poll-instead-of-WebSocket pattern flagged in the live metrics — fleet status is a prime candidate for the existing signed-WS channel.

verdict.reasoning:
The core technical claim is REAL and reachable. The Screens page (apps/web/src/app/[schoolId]/screens/page.tsx:1374-1375) mounts BOTH useScreenGroups() and useScreens(). These are distinct React Query keys (['screen-groups'] vs ['screens']) hitting distinct endpoints, so RQ does NOT dedupe them — both fire on independent 10s intervals. Verified in use-api.ts:22-39 and 122-143: each hook has refetchInterval: 10_000, refetchIntervalInBackground: true, staleTime: 0. So yes, two full-fleet fetches every 10s, and they keep polling while the mobile tab is backgrounded/screen off — a legitimate battery/cellular-data drain.

But several specifics are WRONG or INFLATED, which drops it from P1 to P2:

1. "useScreens may be entirely redundant here" — FALSE. flatScreens (from useScreens) is load-bearing on this page: it drives FleetSummaryStrip counters (L1693), the fleet map's effectiveLatitude/effectiveLongitude/effectiveAddress/geoSource/lastCacheReport (L1706-1721), and ungroupedScreens (L1455). The nested group.screens[] from /screen-groups (a) is computed without the effective* geo fields (those exist ONLY in screens.controller.ts list()), and (b) by definition can't contain UNGROUPED screens. The proposed "pick ONE source of truth (drop useScreens)" fix would break the map and the ungrouped list. The two payloads are NOT equivalent — /screen-groups is actually the HEAVIER one (~25-field nested select per screen incl. OTA/crash/version fields, screen-groups.controller.ts:53-90).

2. The "88%-full Vercel edge budget" tie-in is inaccurate. apiFetch targets the Railway API directly via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL (api-url.ts, api-client.ts:82) — these polls never hit Vercel edge; they consume Railway DB/API load. The headline's resource framing is wrong.

3. Severity: this is a pure efficiency/battery optimization on ONE admin-only page (Screens), not a correctness bug, crash, data loss, or customer-facing/always-mounted surface. The global-shell poller (useTenantStatus) is already correctly throttled to 30s. The genuinely actionable fix is gating refetchIntervalInBackground on document.visibilityState and raising staleTime above 0 to coalesce focus/reconnect refetches — minor mobile polish, not a P1 blocker. No correctness impact, limited blast radius (admin on one page), and the most impactful proposed remedy (dropping useScreens) is itself incorrect.

confirmedCritical.title: Address picker still makes direct browser calls to Nominatim + Photon — third-party data leak, OSM ToS violation, and flaky/CORS-fragile on locked-down networks
confirmedCritical.fix: After the server-side geocodeViaApi() path, the modal falls back to fetching photon.komoot.io and nominatim.openstreetmap.org DIRECTLY from the browser on every keystroke (debounced 300ms). This (a) leaks the operator's typed building address + their IP to two third parties on every search, (b) violates Nominatim's usage policy, which explicitly forbids autocomplete/keystroke querying and an unset Referer/UA from a public app, so it will get rate-limited or blocked at scale, and (c) is the most likely root cause of the 'address picker not finding US addresses' report — these endpoints are frequently blocked by school/corporate firewalls and CORS proxies, and they fail silently to setNoMatch. Move BOTH providers behind the existing /api/v1/geocode proxy (server-side, with a proper User-Agent and the merge/dedupe logic that already exists in the modal) so the only origin the browser talks to is your own API. That also unifies the 'no match' behavior and lets you cache repeat lookups.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL but SEVERITY INFLATED (P1 -> P2). The cited code exists: apps/web/src/components/screens/ScreenLocationModal.tsx:199-216 builds and fetches photon.komoot.io + nominatim.openstreetmap.org directly from the browser, and lines 260-262 do a second direct Nominatim call on Save. The same duplicated pattern lives in apps/web/src/components/ui/AddressAutocomplete.tsx:201-216. So the third-party direct-call code is real and reachable.

However the audit's framing materially overstates the exposure on two points:

1. NOT "on every keystroke." The client-side direct-fetch block runs ONLY when the server proxy geocodeViaApi(q) returns an empty array OR throws (ScreenLocationModal.tsx:174-192 returns early when apiHits.length is truthy). The server proxy (apps/api/src/geocoding/geocoding.service.ts:57-77) ALREADY falls back to Nominatim server-side even when GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is unset (it skips Google and `return this.nominatim(...)`), with a proper User-Agent ('VenueOS-Geocoder/1.0 (+https://venue-os.app)') via safeFetch (DNS-pinned, timeout, byte-capped). So in the normal/default deployment the browser talks ONLY to the own-origin /api/v1/geocode; the direct Photon/Nominatim fetch fires only on the subset of queries the server couldn't resolve, or when the own-origin API itself is unreachable. The IP/typed-address leak and OSM-ToS-violation concerns are genuine but narrow, not per-keystroke.

2. The "most likely root cause of address-picker-not-finding-US-addresses" diagnosis is weak/likely wrong. The proxy is the PRIMARY path and runs Google's authoritative US house-number coverage; the file header comments document that the proxy was added specifically to fix the US-coverage gaps the direct OSM path had. The most probable cause of "not finding addresses" is whether GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is configured server-side, not the browser-side backstop.

3. The proposed fix is partly already implemented. "Move BOTH providers behind the existing /api/v1/geocode proxy" — the proxy exists and already serves Google -> Nominatim. The legitimate RESIDUAL gaps: (a) the client still carries dead-end direct-fetch fallback code that should be deleted, and (b) the server merge does NOT consult Photon at all (geocoding.service.ts only has google() + nominatim()), so the Photon autocomplete coverage the client comments rely on is lost when routed through the proxy — folding Photon into the server merge would be the real improvement.

Net: a real, worthwhile cleanup (remove the client direct fetches in both files; optionally add Photon to the server-side merge), but the privacy/ToS exposure is conditional and infrequent and the picker works via own-origin proxy in the common case, so this is not a mobile launch-blocker. Downgrade to P2. Relevant files: /Users/gschiemann/Desktop/EDU CMS/apps/web/src/components/screens/ScreenLocationModal.tsx, /Users/gschiemann/Desktop/EDU CMS/apps/web/src/components/ui/AddressAutocomplete.tsx, /Users/gschiemann/Desktop/EDU CMS/apps/web/src/lib/geocode.ts, /Users/gschiemann/Desktop/EDU CMS/apps/api/src/geocoding/geocoding.service.ts, /Users/gschiemann/Desktop/EDU CMS/apps/api/src/geocoding/geocoding.controller.ts.

confirmedCritical.title: cache-status + render-proof telemetry do an unconditional Screen UPDATE every 30s with no debounce — ~59% of all DB time
evidence: apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3242-3248 (reportCacheStatus: unconditional screen.update of lastCacheReport JSON + lastCacheReportAt every call, no shouldSkipLastPingWrite, no @Throttle)

apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3302-3309 (reportRenderProof: unconditional screen.update of lastRenderedAt every call; @Throttle 10/min exists but does not reduce the steady-state 30s write)
apps/api/src/screens/manifest-hot-cache.ts:82-94 (shouldSkipLastPingWrite/markLastPingWritten debounce that the ping+manifest paths use but these two endpoints do NOT)
LIVE pg_stat_statements: UPDATE screens last_cache_report = 41.6% of DB time / 180826 calls; UPDATE screens last_rendered_at = 17.4% / 161168 calls
confirmedCritical.fix: The cache-status payload is identical on ~99% of polls (cache contents rarely change) and render-proof only needs server-clock freshness, so both are writing the same value every 30s. (1) cache-status: gate the write behind a same-as-last-value check (compare the new JSON to the stored lastCacheReport; skip the update when unchanged, OR add a 5-minute debounce keyed by screenId in manifest-hot-cache.ts — admin visibility tolerates 5-min staleness fine) and raise the client cadence to 5 min. (2) render-proof: apply the existing 25s shouldSkipLastPingWrite-style debounce (a fresh-enough lastRenderedAt does not need re-writing every 30s; a 60-90s debounce keeps the render-STALE threshold accurate) and/or use a raw `UPDATE ... SET last_rendered_at = now() WHERE id = $1` to avoid Prisma's full-row rewrite. Either change alone removes the bulk of the 59% DB-time spend with zero behavioral regression.

verdict.reasoning:
REAL and reachable. Both endpoints do an unconditional, un-debounced full-row Prisma screen.update every 30s on every paired screen:
- cache-status: screens.controller.ts:3242-3248 writes lastCacheReport(JSON) + lastCacheReportAt with no shouldSkipLastPingWrite and no @Throttle.
- render-proof: screens.controller.ts:3302-3309 writes lastRenderedAt every call; the @Throttle(10/60s) is a flood ceiling, not a steady-state reducer — at 30s cadence the player only hits 2/min, so the throttle never engages.
- Client cadences confirmed unconditional setInterval(post,30_000) at player/page.tsx:2413 (cache-status) and :2531 (render-proof). (render-proof has a client-side frames===lastReportedFrames skip, but that only suppresses writes during an actual freeze; steady-state the frame counter advances every poll, so it writes every 30s.)
- The debounce infra (shouldSkipLastPingWrite/markLastPingWritten, 25s) exists in manifest-hot-cache.ts:82-94 and IS wired into the ping/manifest paths (controller 662-666, 2493-2494) but NOT these two endpoints — exactly as evidenced. The pg_stat_statements split (41.6%+17.4%≈59%) is consistent with the cited call counts. Confirmed P1.

CAVEAT — the proposed cache-status remedy is UNSAFE as written and the fix author missed a dependency: ScreenWedgeDetectorCron (screen-wedge-detector.cron.ts:160,176; CACHE_REPORT_STALE_MS = 5*60_000) uses a continuously-fresh lastCacheReportAt as a LOAD-BEARING liveness proof — a still-pinging screen whose lastCacheReportAt goes >5min stale is classified as renderer-wedged and gets a forced REFRESH_WEB. Therefore (a) 'skip the write when the JSON is unchanged' would leave lastCacheReportAt stale on healthy screens (cache contents rarely change — the audit's own premise) → false wedge detection → spurious full-page reloads on healthy kiosks; and (b) 'raise client cadence to 5min' parks the timestamp on the 5-min stale boundary → intermittent false fires. The safe fix keeps the timestamp moving on every poll (sub-5-min debounce, e.g. ~2min, or a raw UPDATE ... SET last_cache_report_at=now() that still stamps the time but skips the JSON-blob rewrite), never skip-on-unchanged.

The render-proof half is sound but the debounce must be capped BELOW the 90s STALE threshold (render-proof.ts:38, RENDER_PROOF_STALE_MS = 90*1000): the suggested '60-90s' must be ~60s, since a 90s debounce races the threshold and would false-RED a healthy screen. The raw-SQL timestamp-only UPDATE suggestion is correct.

Net: confirmed real P1 (DB-time spend is genuine and the missing debounce is the cause), but the remediation cannot be applied verbatim — the skip-on-unchanged cache-status variant would introduce a behavioral regression (false kiosk reloads + false RED render health) via the wedge-detector and render-stale thresholds.

confirmedCritical.title: Three overlapping GET /screens/status heartbeats per playing kiosk (web 30s + web 45s + native 30s) — redundant network + Vercel edge-request pressure
evidence: apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:3625 (playing-phase httpHeartbeat, setInterval 45_000 — runs concurrently with the always-on loop once phase==='playing')
LIVE Vercel: Edge Requests 887K/1M (88%) — every /api/v1/* is rewritten through Vercel edge
confirmedCritical.fix: In the playing phase the always-on 30s loop already covers liveness, so the additional 45s playing-phase ping at page.tsx:3617-3625 is pure duplication — remove it (the always-on loop's handleHeartbeatOta already processes the OTA fields). For the APK, the native HeartbeatService duplicates the WebView heartbeat; pick ONE (prefer the native one since it survives a wedged WebView) and have the web side skip its own /status ping when running inside the APK (the EduCmsNative bridge is already detected elsewhere). Net: ~3 status GETs/min/kiosk → 1, directly trimming both Vercel edge requests and pooled DB read load at fleet scale.

verdict.reasoning:
The core factual claim is REAL and reachable. On a playing APK kiosk, three independent /screens/status GET loops fire concurrently: (1) the always-on 30s loop at apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:3457-3478, (2) the playing-phase 45s httpHeartbeat at page.tsx:3605-3625, and (3) the native Kotlin HeartbeatService 30s loop at HeartbeatService.kt:171-186. All three are gated ONLY by isPreviewMode() / fingerprint presence — none is gated by isAndroidWebView() — so inside the APK all three run. The web playing-phase ping (3617-3625) is genuinely pure duplication: it await-fetches /status and DISCARDS the response, whereas the always-on loop (3470) already calls handleHeartbeatOta on the same response. Removing 3617-3625 is correct and safe. (Note: actual per-kiosk rate is ~5.3 GETs/min, not the "3/min" the FIX text states.)

BUT the severity is INFLATED to P1, and the headline cost driver is a MISATTRIBUTION:

1. Vercel edge requests — the claim's strongest "evidence" (Edge Requests 887K/1M, "every /api/v1/* is rewritten through Vercel edge") does NOT apply to this traffic. The player fetches via getApiRoot() (page.tsx:547-561) which returns NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL — the Railway API origin — DIRECTLY. The vercel.json rewrite (/api/v1/:path* → Railway) only fires for requests to the Vercel ORIGIN; the player and the native Kotlin loop both hit api-production-39a1.up.railway.app directly, bypassing Vercel edge entirely (this was the explicit subject of completed task #212 / AUDIT-P0-4 "player route bypasses CDN proxy"). So these heartbeats consume ZERO Vercel edge requests. The 887K figure is unrelated dashboard/browser traffic.

2. DB load — every /status GET is one indexed findUnique READ, but the lastPingAt WRITE is debounced server-side to once/25s/screen via shouldSkipLastPingWrite + LAST_PING_DEBOUNCE_MS (manifest-hot-cache.ts:35,82-86; wired at screens.controller.ts:662-675). The real write-amplification P0 here (3s polling × 3 round-trips ≈ 43M queries/day) was already fixed (controller comment 630-646). Residual is a few extra cheap reads, not pool contention.

3. The recommended fix ("pick ONE, prefer native") collides with intentional design: the native HeartbeatService exists to survive a wedged WebView (its docstring), and screen-wedge-detector.cron.ts deliberately cross-checks the native vs web ping timers as a liveness signal — collapsing to one timer would weaken that detector.

Verdict: real, low-grade efficiency redundancy; the duplicate 45s web ping at 3617-3625 is a safe removal. But it's a P2 cleanup, not a P1 — the Vercel-edge amplifier is misattributed, the DB-write cost is already debounced, and the native/web overlap is partly intentional.

confirmedCritical.title: Player telemetry writes (cache-status + render-proof) are undebounced — 59% of all DB time
evidence: apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3242-3248 (cache-status: unconditional screen.update on every 30s POST, no debounce, no withDbRetry)
apps/api/src/screens/manifest-hot-cache.ts:82-94 (the shouldSkipLastPingWrite debounce that lastPingAt uses but these two endpoints do NOT)
confirmedCritical.fix: These two endpoints write the same `screens` row that lastPingAt already keeps fresh, but with zero coalescing — live pg_stat_statements shows them at 41.6% (180,826 calls, 19.84ms mean) and 17.4% (161,168 calls, 9.33ms mean) of total DB time. Apply the existing debounce pattern: gate both writes behind a per-screen `shouldSkip*Write(id)` check (e.g. 60-120s window for cache-status, which only feeds an admin visibility pill, and ~90s for render-proof, whose staleness threshold is minutes not seconds). Keep the freshest in-memory value and flush on the debounce boundary. This is a ~5-10× reduction on the two hottest queries with no loss of signal fidelity, mirroring the lastPingAt fix already shipped. Also wrap both in withDbRetry for parity with the heartbeat path. The 9-20ms mean on a single-row update of a 76-column table also points at lock contention from these concurrent same-row writers — debouncing directly relieves it.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — real, reachable, and correctly P1. Verified against code:

(1) cache-status (apps/api/src/screens/screens.controller.ts:3242-3248): unconditional `prisma.client.screen.update` on every POST. No debounce, no withDbRetry, AND no @Throttle decorator at all (uncapped even at the rate-limit layer).

(2) render-proof (3302-3309): same unconditional `screen.update`, no debounce, no withDbRetry. The audit omitted that it DOES carry @Throttle({limit:10, ttl:60_000}), but at the ~30s player cadence (≤2 POST/min) that throttle never engages, so it's not a meaningful mitigation of write volume. (Player does skip the POST when the rAF frame counter is frozen, line 2513 — but in normal operation it writes every 30s.)

(3) Player cadence confirmed: cache-status setInterval(30_000) at apps/web/src/app/player/page.tsx:2413; render-proof setInterval(30_000) at 2531; both also fire once on mount.

(4) The debounce infra it should use is real and already wired into the two SIBLING write paths: shouldSkipLastPingWrite/markLastPingWritten (manifest-hot-cache.ts:82-94, 25s window) gate the heartbeat write (controller:662-666) and the manifest lastPingAt write. These two telemetry endpoints write the SAME `screens` row that lastPingAt already keeps fresh, but bypass the debounce entirely. The architectural inconsistency and the proposed fix (mirror the lastPingAt debounce + wrap in withDbRetry) are exactly right and follow an established in-repo pattern.

confirmedCritical.title: JWT revocation check fails OPEN when Redis is down, contradicting the 'fail-closed' guard comment
evidence: apps/api/src/auth/jwt-auth.guard.ts:97-126 (comment: 'Now we fail CLOSED ... if we can't confirm the token isn't revoked, we deny')
confirmedCritical.fix: The guard's try/catch only fails-closed on THROWN errors, but sismember() swallows the Redis-down case and returns false (= 'not revoked'), and getTokenInvalidBefore() returns null (= 'no mass-revocation marker') — so when Redis is unavailable, a logged-out or demoted user's token keeps working. That directly contradicts the documented intent. Decide the posture explicitly: either make sismember/getTokenInvalidBefore throw a distinguishable RedisUnavailableError when `!connected` so the guard's existing catch fails closed (it already maps to 'Auth check unavailable; please retry'), or keep fail-open but update the guard comment to stop claiming fail-closed. For a life-safety/multi-tenant product, failing closed on revocation is the correct call.

verdict.reasoning:
REAL and reachable, but severity is inflated from P1 to P2. I traced every path.

THE CONTRADICTION IS REAL. jwt-auth.guard.ts:97-126 wraps the two revocation reads in a try/catch that only fails CLOSED on a THROWN error. But redis.service.ts:172-176 (`sismember`) returns `false` without throwing when `!this.connected || !this.publisher`, and :240-247 (`getTokenInvalidBefore`) returns `null` without throwing when `!this.publisher`. So when Redis is NOT configured (publisher===null — a deploy mode CLAUDE.md explicitly supports: "Redis missing → API boots anyway"), neither read throws, the guard's catch never fires, and a demoted/logged-out user's token keeps its claim for up to 30d. That directly contradicts the guard comment ("Now we fail CLOSED") and the users.controller.ts:81-84 comment ("the guard itself fails CLOSED on Redis errors, so a Redis outage can't be the thing that lets a stale token through"). The jwt-auth.guard.spec.ts tests only the mocked-THROW case (sismemberThrows/invalidBeforeThrows) — they never exercise the real RedisService !connected/!publisher branches, so the fail-open is untested.

WHY THE CLAIM IS PARTLY IMPRECISE / SEVERITY IS INFLATED:
1. The claim says blanket fail-open "when Redis is unavailable." That's only true in the Redis-NOT-CONFIGURED mode (publisher===null). When Redis IS configured but DOWN (publisher!==null, stream not writeable), getTokenInvalidBefore's unguarded `.get()` at line 248 actually REJECTS — I verified ioredis@5.10.1 with enableOfflineQueue:false throws "Stream isn't writeable and enableOfflineQueue options is false" (built/Redis.js:364-365). That rejection propagates to the guard's catch → fails CLOSED for user tokens. So a real mid-life Redis outage on a Redis-configured deploy fails closed for the mass-revocation (privilege-tightening) path; only the sismember single-token logout path fails open.
2. In Redis-less mode, logout itself returns 503 (auth.controller.ts:169-174) and markUserTokensInvalid throws (redis.service.ts:220-221), so "a logged-out token keeps working" is largely moot — the logout never registers. The real residual exposure is the DEMOTION path: revokeUserTokens (users.controller.ts:88-97) swallows the throw, reports success, and the stale elevated/canTriggerPanic claim survives up to 30d.
3. DB row remains the durable source of truth; this is a token-staleness window, not an auth bypass.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE FOR P2: the codebase's own prior audits already found this exact issue and rated it P2. docs/research/2026-06-09-prelaunch-final-audit/07-auth-identity.md:50-52 documents it and states verbatim: "Live reality check: prod /health currently shows redis:'ok', so the window is latent, not active today. That's why this is P2, not P1." The 2026-06-08 synthesis logged the same finding (P1-8) but the later dedicated auth audit explicitly downgraded it to P2 on the basis that production runs with REDIS_URL set and healthy. Given prod Redis is present/healthy (latent window), the narrow blast radius (Redis-less prod OR a configured-Redis outage hitting only the logout-token path), and the DB staying source-of-truth, P2 is correct, not P1. The recommended fix matches the claim and prior audits: add a strict throwing variant (or correct the comment) AND boot-WARN when REDIS_URL is unset + re-read canTriggerPanic/role from the live DB inside the @AllowPanicBypass branch so the emergency path can't fire on a stale claim.

confirmedCritical.title: Floor-plan images stored in a PUBLIC Supabase bucket; signed-URL read path is a fig leaf
evidence: apps/api/src/floor-plans/floor-plans.controller.ts:463-468 (comment 'if it ever escapes the public bucket', `publicUrl = await this.storage.upload(...)`)
task #200 still pending: 'Move floor-plan objects to a PRIVATE Supabase bucket (full F-1 fix)'
confirmedCritical.fix: Floor plans are sensitive (building layouts used for emergency/lockdown response). They upload to a public bucket, so the createSignedUrl TTL on the read path provides no real confidentiality — the object is reachable by anyone with the public URL (leaked via logs, referrer, browser history, or path-guessing within the tenant prefix). Move floor-plan storage to a private bucket and serve exclusively via short-TTL signed URLs (the read path already does this). The tenant-scoped path only mitigates blind guessing, not URL leakage.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — real, reachable, and correctly severity-rated. Verified against the cited code and the storage layer:

1. The single Supabase bucket `assets` is created AND updated with `public: true` (apps/api/src/storage/supabase-storage.service.ts:81 and :96). No SQL migration / RLS policy gates it — I grepped packages/database and apps/api/src/storage; the only "policy" references are the bucket-level MIME/size allowlist, not row-level access control. So every object in this bucket is world-readable by anyone holding (or able to derive) its URL, with no auth.

2. Floor plans upload to that same public bucket: apps/api/src/floor-plans/floor-plans.controller.ts:467-470 builds path `${tenantId}/floor-plans/${Date.now()}-${rand6}.${ext}` and calls `this.storage.upload(...)`, which returns `${url}/storage/v1/object/public/${BUCKET}/${filePath}` (supabase-storage.service.ts:237). That permanent public URL is persisted to the DB `imageUrl` column (controller:498). The upload comment itself concedes "if it ever escapes the public bucket."

3. The read path (`withSignedImageUrl`, controller:238-243, used by list/getOne/create) re-derives the path and issues a short-TTL `createSignedUrl` (default TTL constant ~300s), so clients only ever receive the signed form, never the permanent public URL. This is the genuine mitigation the claim acknowledges — and it is exactly a fig leaf for confidentiality: a signed URL is just the same object plus `?token=`; an attacker who captures a signed URL (logs, referrer, browser history, proxy) can strip the token and hit the permanent `…/object/public/…` form, which the public bucket serves forever regardless of TTL. The TTL only limits replay of the signed link, not the underlying object's public reachability.

4. Task #200 ("Move floor-plan objects to a PRIVATE Supabase bucket (full F-1 fix)") is genuinely still pending in the task list. The fix the claim prescribes (private bucket + signed-only serving; read path already exists) is exactly the right and unimplemented remediation.

Severity: P1 is defensible and I'm keeping it. The data is K-12 building layouts with per-screen pin locations used for lockdown/evacuation response — high-sensitivity operational-security data; the prior infra audit (docs/research/2026-05-28-opus48-audit/37) rated this F-1 as a P1 launch-blocker "IF floor plans are in launch scope." Two caveats that pull it toward the P1/P2 boundary, which I note rather than downgrade on: (a) the permanent public URL never leaves the server (clients get the signed form), so there is no direct referrer/history leak of the permanent URL — the exposure requires a captured signed URL as a precondition; and (b) blind path enumeration is effectively infeasible (tenant UUID + 13-digit ms timestamp + 36^6 random suffix). A later audit (2026-06-09 sonnet-baseline) rated the same finding P2 for these reasons. Net: it is a real, unfixed confidentiality control gap on sensitive emergency-response data, with a meaningful (signed-URL-leak) attack path; P1 is appropriate, sitting at the upper edge given the precondition.
